**Question.** Was the 2026-09-12 closure right that 20 tok/s per stream at c8
needs new hardware or a smaller checkpoint?

No. The closure overgeneralized, and the EXL3 stack falsified it the same day.

| claim in the closure | status |
| --- | --- |
| no-spec c8 floor, pair 103 ms / single 166 ms | stands (measured) |
| spec net-negative with per-token-step verify (75 vs 78 agg at k=2) | stands, for that verify design |
| spec net-negative, period | **wrong** - verify that reads weights once per chunk flips it |
| reopen needs new hardware or a smaller checkpoint | **wrong** - reopen needs chunked verify, which the EXL3 stack already had |

The confounder: "on this checkpoint" conflated the fuel with the engine's
verify design. The EXL3 vLLM pair, running the same base model with trellis
4bpw experts and a chunked-prefill verify (weights read once per layer for
all k+1 positions, recurrence unrolled in-kernel), measured 20.84 tok/s per
stream at c8 with DFlash2 k=3 - above the closed target, on the same 236 GB/s
box, no hardware change.

The mechanism was documented in the campaign's own protocol notes before the
closure was written; the closure's verdict line failed to carry it.

**Corrected statement.** On the NVFP4 fuel with the one-token-per-step engine,
20 tok/s per stream at c8 is unreachable within quality gates - that part is
measured and stands. With chunked verify and a draft model, the token rate
multiplies by the acceptance length at sublinear byte cost, and the target is
reachable: the EXL3 stack demonstrates it, and the CUDA engine rebuilt on the
EXL3 expert fuel (12.6 MiB slots, fp8-row non-expert at 7.3 GB - lighter than
the vLLM stack's BF16 non-expert set) predicts 22 to 25 tok/s per stream at
c8. The build is scoped in the glm53-dflash2-cuda-engine skill.

**Verdict.** Accepted as a correction. The reopen condition for the c8 target
is the chunked-verify build, not hardware.
